answer.diagnosis: getLiveIntervals follows descriptor views but stops at arith.select, so backing allocations can expire before the selected descriptor's load. In case-24/25, the temporary occupies columns [0,64), overlapping both selected candidates; all selected outputs become 7 (fact-24/26). With a 32-column temporary, only the candidate at column 0 is overwritten: case-27 fails while case-26 passes (fact-29/27). Early allocation avoids overlap and passes (case-30/31, fact-33/35). The repair transitively merges select-result liveness, including chained selects and intervening views, with a visited set to avoid repeated traversal at converging paths. It preserves first-fit placement, alignment, row constraints, and reuse after actual last use; the direct-first control's reuse of the dead second allocation remains legal (case-32, fact-36/37). Limitations: static IR does not establish GPU timestamps; compilation and runtime validation of this proposed edit were unavailable.
